Part of the problem in conservative media right now is that everyone is just repeating the same 3 or 4 political talking points over and over again. It’s boring and the audience is exhausted by it. Cultural analysis takes more time to research and think about, and there isn’t a predetermined position you’re supposed to take based on your “team,” so most people in the space avoid it. But that’s what makes it interesting and fun.

I did a deep dive into the death of rock music. I wasn’t sure how interested the audience would be, but I personally think it’s a fascinating topic and important so I went with it. Turns out the audience agrees. 300k views on a 45 minute monologue.

When we were filming What Is A Woman, I watched the Masai slaughter a goat and then I ate its kidneys raw (not bad actually, very mild taste). I’ve come to realize that the goat community has been exacting its revenge on me ever since.
Which recipe should I go with?

My wife has acquired another goat. This is goat number three. She tells me that three goats will be enough but I’m starting to be skeptical. I have become a full time goat herder. This is who I am now. It has always been my fate. There’s no escaping it.

Scam texts and calls are totally out of control. And they’re getting very sophisticated. You might still be able to identify the scams right away but it’s not so easy for your grandma. It’s going to get so much worse with AI. Now’s the time for an extreme crackdown. Scammers should get the death penalty. We should be doing drone strikes on the scammer compounds in Asia and Africa. Treat it like a national security issue, because it obviously is.

Kevin James is the Judge, just to be clear. The Kid will be portrayed by the black girl from the Little Mermaid remake. She’s a tough no nonsense chick and she’s not taking any flak from that bumbling Judge or anyone else. Toadvine is the comedic relief (“Toady,” they call him) played by Kevin Hart. The adaptation will go on to make 12 dollars in the box office and then win 46 Academy Awards.

Everyone’s complaining about the fact that this Animal Farm movie undercuts Orwell’s critique of communism, which is true. But, message aside, I think it’s just as bad that they’ve taken a serious and intelligent story and turned it into a goofy slapstick farce complete with fart jokes. It’s like making a Crime and Punishment adaptation and turning it into a romantic comedy. No respect for the source material at all. A cynical cash grab.
